title: Training & Fine-tuning
blurb: How a base model becomes a useful product. Pretraining at a glance, then the fine-tuning techniques that actually fit on a single engineer's GPU budget: SFT, instruction tuning, RLHF, DPO, LoRA, distillation.

nodes.label: The pretraining pipeline (overview)
nodes.description: Data, tokenization, mixed-precision training, optimizer state, checkpointing, the scale. You will not pretrain a frontier model — but you should understand the pipeline you're inheriting.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the end-to-end pretraining pipeline at a level that lets you read a model card.

resources.title: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
resources.author: Groeneveld et al. (AI2)
resources.annotation: The open, fully-documented pretraining recipe. Code, data, checkpoints, and all the engineering decisions written down.

resources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
resources.author: Meta AI
resources.annotation: The closest thing to a fully-documented frontier pretraining recipe outside Anthropic / OpenAI. The data section alone is education.

nodes.label: Data curation
nodes.description: Filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixing ratios, contamination. In 2026, data work is the highest-leverage thing most fine-tuners do.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a small SFT dataset and defend each filtering and mixing choice.

resources.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
resources.author: Gao et al. (EleutherAI)
resources.annotation: The first openly-documented large-scale pretraining dataset. Read for the mixing-ratio discussion alone.

resources.title: Textbooks Are All You Need
resources.author: Gunasekar et al. (Microsoft)
resources.annotation: The Phi-series paper that put data quality on the map. The case for 'fewer, higher-quality tokens' over 'more tokens'.

resources.title: Hugging Face — FineWeb
resources.annotation: Detailed walk-through of curating a 15T-token pretraining dataset. The most accessible data-curation case study published.

nodes.label: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
nodes.description: Take a base model, train it on prompt-response pairs. The bread and butter of most adaptation work today.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run an SFT pass on a small open-weights model and evaluate the result.

resources.title: Hugging Face — Supervised Fine-Tuning (TRL)
resources.annotation: The TRL library's SFTTrainer is the production default. The docs are a working tutorial.

resources.title: Axolotl
resources.annotation: The community-default config-driven fine-tuning wrapper. Read the example configs; you'll learn the practical knobs.

nodes.label: Instruction tuning
nodes.description: SFT with instruction-following data, multi-task and multi-format. Why every base model needs this before it's product-shaped.
nodes.doneWhen: You can distinguish a base model from an instruction-tuned one by their outputs.

resources.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback (InstructGPT)
resources.author: Ouyang et al. (OpenAI)
resources.annotation: The paper that defined the modern alignment pipeline: SFT, reward modeling, RLHF. The starting point for everything that followed.

resources.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
resources.author: Wang et al.
resources.annotation: The bootstrap data-synthesis recipe that put Alpaca-style fine-tuning on the map. Still the simplest path to a usable instruction dataset.

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.description: Reward model + PPO, the InstructGPT recipe. Still the conceptual reference even where it's been replaced by simpler methods.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the RLHF loop end-to-end and identify its three training stages.

resources.title: Illustrating Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
resources.author: Hugging Face
resources.annotation: The accessible illustrated explainer of the three-stage RLHF pipeline. Read this before the original paper.

resources.title: TRL — Transformer Reinforcement Learning
resources.annotation: The library you'd actually use to run PPO, DPO, GRPO. The implementations are the cleanest open reference.

nodes.label: DPO & direct preference methods
nodes.description: Direct Preference Optimization and the family of reward-model-free preference methods. The pragmatic default for preference learning in 2026.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why DPO simplified preference training versus RLHF and where it falls short.

resources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
resources.author: Rafailov et al.
resources.annotation: The DPO paper. Closed-form policy update, no reward model, no PPO. Short and worth re-reading.

resources.title: Hugging Face — DPO Trainer
resources.annotation: Production-shaped DPO. The 'how to actually run it' page; pair with the paper for the why.

resources.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
resources.author: Ethayarajh et al.
resources.annotation: KTO trains on unpaired signals (good / bad), not pairs. The right answer when collecting paired preferences is impractical.

nodes.label: LoRA / QLoRA / adapters
nodes.description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Why you can fine-tune a 7B+ model on a single consumer GPU and why low-rank decomposition works.
nodes.doneWhen: You can fine-tune an open-weights model with LoRA on a single GPU and explain the rank/alpha trade-offs.

resources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
resources.author: Hu et al.
resources.annotation: The LoRA paper. Eight pages; the math is approachable and the empirical results changed how the field fine-tunes.

resources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
resources.author: Dettmers et al.
resources.annotation: Quantize the base to 4-bit, train LoRA on top. The combination that puts 65B fine-tunes on a single A6000.

resources.title: Hugging Face PEFT — Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
resources.annotation: The library. LoRA, QLoRA, prefix tuning, and friends, with one-line APIs. The reference for the practical knobs.

nodes.label: Distillation & model compression
nodes.description: Teacher-student training, distillation from a larger model into a smaller one, why this is the only practical path to cheap-fast specialized models.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe a distillation setup and identify when it's the right tool versus SFT.

resources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
resources.author: Hinton, Vinyals, Dean
resources.annotation: The original distillation paper. Eight pages; the temperature trick is still relevant to every modern LLM-distillation recipe.

resources.title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT
resources.author: Sanh et al. (Hugging Face)
resources.annotation: The canonical 'distill a transformer' recipe. The architecture is dated but the recipe transfers to modern LLMs.

nodes.label: Evaluation during training
nodes.description: Loss is not evaluation. Train-time evals: holdout sets, regression tests, mid-run sanity checks, the eval suite you need before you fine-tune anything serious.
nodes.doneWhen: You set up a meaningful eval suite before kicking off your first fine-tuning run, not after.

resources.title: Eleuther — lm-evaluation-harness
resources.annotation: The standard harness for running benchmarks. Wire one regression-test task into your training loop on day one.

resources.title: What We Learned from a Year of Building with LLMs
resources.author: Yan, Bryan, et al.
resources.annotation: The collective wisdom from six practitioners. The section on evals is the best 'why your loss isn't enough' argument in print.

nodes.label: Distributed training infrastructure
nodes.description: Data parallel, tensor parallel, pipeline parallel, ZeRO / FSDP. How a frontier model trains across thousands of GPUs.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe FSDP's sharding strategy and explain when tensor parallelism is required.

resources.title: PyTorch FSDP — Getting Started
resources.annotation: The official tutorial. FSDP is the default distributed strategy in 2026; this is the right place to start.

resources.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
resources.author: Rajbhandari et al. (DeepSpeed)
resources.annotation: The ZeRO paper. The three stages of sharding (optimizer / gradients / parameters) are the foundation of every modern strategy.

resources.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook
resources.author: Hugging Face
resources.annotation: An interactive guide to the parallelism strategies of large-scale training. The most accessible map of the distributed-training landscape.
